<!-- Generated by scripts/build_help.py from Puzzle's own data: don't edit. -->


Shared settings live on each solve step; a solver's own settings live on the study (Properties → Solver settings). Only what is set is written, so a default never moves a result. Past these, a checked pass-through takes the solver's own keywords (Expert settings).

<!-- key: setting:shared -->
## Shared by every solver

<!-- key: setting:shared:linear_solver, setting:linear_solver -->
### Linear solver

`linear_solver`; a choice; default 'direct'; for every step.
Choices: Direct (robust; memory grows fast with size) (`direct`), Iterative (large models) (`iterative`).

How each linear system is solved; each solver uses its own direct or iterative method.

<!-- key: setting:shared:tolerance, setting:tolerance -->
### Relative tolerance

`tolerance`; a number; default 1e-06; for every step.

When a nonlinear solve has converged: the residual relative to the loads.

<!-- key: setting:shared:max_iterations, setting:max_iterations -->
### Iteration limit

`max_iterations`; an integer; default 50; for every step.

Nonlinear iterations allowed per increment.

<!-- key: setting:shared:output_every, setting:output_every -->
### Output every

`output_every`; an integer; default 1; in increments; for every step.

Keep results every n-th increment or time step.

<!-- key: setting:shared:increments, setting:increments -->
### Load increments

`increments`; an integer; for stationary.

The load goes in over this many increments at most (the largest increment is 1/n of the load). More help a model that will not converge; each increment's results are kept.

<!-- key: setting:shared:initial_increment, setting:initial_increment -->
### First increment

`initial_increment`; a number; at most 1; for stationary.

The first increment as a fraction of the load (0.1 starts with a tenth); smaller helps contact settle.

<!-- key: setting:shared:min_increment, setting:min_increment -->
### Smallest increment

`min_increment`; a number; at most 1; for stationary.

How far an increment may be cut back (a fraction of the load) before the solve stops.

<!-- key: setting:shared:fixed_increments, setting:fixed_increments -->
### Fixed increments

`fixed_increments`; a bool; default False; for stationary.

Every increment the same size, never cut back or grown: a failed increment ends the solve.

<!-- key: setting:calculix -->
## CalculiX

<!-- key: setting:calculix:solver -->
### Linear solver

`solver`, the solver's `SOLVER=`; a choice; default 'default'; for every step.
Choices: CalculiX's choice (PARDISO if built in, else SPOOLES) (`default`), SPOOLES (direct) (`SPOOLES`), PARDISO (direct, if built in) (`PARDISO`), Iterative, Cholesky preconditioner (`ITERATIVE CHOLESKY`), Iterative, diagonal scaling (`ITERATIVE SCALING`).

The equation solver on each step's procedure card; iterative ones suit large static models.

<!-- key: setting:calculix:cutbacks -->
### Cut-backs per increment

`cutbacks`, the solver's `*CONTROLS I_A`; an integer; default 5; for stationary.

How many times an increment that does not converge is cut back and tried again before the solve stops.

<!-- key: setting:calculix:cutback_factor -->
### Cut-back factor

`cutback_factor`, the solver's `*CONTROLS D_f`; a number; default 0.25; at most 0.99; for stationary.

A failed increment is retried at this fraction of its size.

<!-- key: setting:calculix:increase_factor -->
### Growth factor

`increase_factor`, the solver's `*CONTROLS D_D`; a number; default 1.5; for stationary.

An increment that converges easily is followed by one this much larger (up to the largest increment).

<!-- key: setting:calculix:reduce_after -->
### Shrink after

`reduce_after`, the solver's `*CONTROLS I_L`; an integer; default 10; in iterations; for stationary; shown at the power-user level.

An increment taking more iterations than this is converged, but the next one is made smaller.

<!-- key: setting:calculix:divergence_check_after -->
### Divergence check after

`divergence_check_after`, the solver's `*CONTROLS I_0`; an integer; default 4; in iterations; for stationary; shown at the power-user level.

From this iteration on, residuals growing in two iterations running cut the increment back; larger is more patient with contact.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster -->
## Code_Aster

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:method -->
### Linear solver

`method`, the solver's `SOLVEUR/METHODE`; a choice; default 'MUMPS'; for every step.
Choices: MUMPS (direct, the default) (`MUMPS`), Multifrontal (direct, Code_Aster's own) (`MULT_FRONT`), Preconditioned conjugate gradient (iterative) (`GCPC`), PETSc (iterative; parallel Code_Aster builds only) (`PETSC`).

The method for every linear system; iterative ones suit large models and take a preconditioner Code_Aster chooses.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:acceleration -->
### MUMPS acceleration

`acceleration`, the solver's `SOLVEUR/ACCELERATION`; a choice; default 'AUTO'; for every step.
Choices: Code_Aster's choice (`AUTO`), Full rank (exact) (`FR`), Full rank, faster (exact) (`FR+`), Low rank (to a tolerance) (`LR`), Low rank, faster (to a tolerance) (`LR+`).

Full rank is exact; low rank compresses the factors to the tolerance below, often several times faster on large 3D solids.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:low_rank_threshold -->
### Low-rank tolerance

`low_rank_threshold`, the solver's `SOLVEUR/LOW_RANK_SEUIL`; a number; default 0.0; for every step; shown at the power-user level.

How far low-rank factors may differ (relative): 1e-9 keeps results to about that, larger is faster; 0 lets MUMPS decide.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:ordering -->
### MUMPS ordering

`ordering`, the solver's `SOLVEUR/RENUM`; a choice; default 'AUTO'; for every step; shown at the power-user level.
Choices: Code_Aster's choice (`AUTO`), METIS (`METIS`), SCOTCH (`SCOTCH`), PORD (`PORD`), Approximate minimum degree (AMD) (`AMD`), Approximate minimum fill (AMF) (`AMF`), Quasi-dense AMD (QAMD) (`QAMD`).

How the unknowns are numbered before factoring; it sets the factors' size. METIS suits large 3D meshes.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:refinement -->
### MUMPS refinement

`refinement`, the solver's `SOLVEUR/POSTTRAITEMENTS`; a choice; default 'FORCE'; for every step; shown at the power-user level.
Choices: Always (keeps the accuracy check; Puzzle's default) (`FORCE`), Code_Aster's choice (`AUTO`), Off (`SANS`).

Iterative refinement after the solve, so large models pass Code_Aster's accuracy check (1e-6) instead of stopping with FACTOR_57; it costs a few per cent of the solve.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:factor_memory -->
### MUMPS factors kept

`factor_memory`, the solver's `SOLVEUR/GESTION_MEMOIRE`; a choice; default 'AUTO'; for every step; shown at the power-user level.
Choices: Code_Aster's choice (`AUTO`), In memory (fastest) (`IN_CORE`), On disk (least memory) (`OUT_OF_CORE`).

In memory is fastest when they fit; on disk lets a large model run in less memory.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:reac_iter -->
### Tangent matrix every

`reac_iter`, the solver's `NEWTON/REAC_ITER`; an integer; default 1; in iterations; for every step; shown at the power-user level.

How often a nonlinear solve rebuilds its tangent matrix: 1 every iteration (robust), more to save time when it converges easily.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:line_search -->
### Line search

`line_search`, the solver's `RECH_LINEAIRE/METHODE`; a choice; default 'none'; for every step.
Choices: None (Code_Aster's default) (`none`), Secant (CORDE) (`CORDE`), Mixed: bracketing, then secant (MIXTE) (`MIXTE`).

Scales each Newton correction to lower the residual: helps contact, plasticity and large deflection that overshoot or oscillate.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:line_search_iterations -->
### Line search iterations

`line_search_iterations`, the solver's `RECH_LINEAIRE/ITER_LINE_MAXI`; an integer; default 3; for every step; shown at the power-user level.

Trials per line search; more for a residual that is hard to lower.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:prediction -->
### Prediction

`prediction`, the solver's `NEWTON/PREDICTION`; a choice; default 'default'; for every step.
Choices: Code_Aster's choice (tangent) (`default`), Tangent (`TANGENTE`), Elastic (`ELASTIQUE`), Extrapolated from the last increment (`EXTRAPOLE`).

How each increment's first guess is made; elastic is the most robust start for plasticity and contact.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:matrix -->
### Newton matrix

`matrix`, the solver's `NEWTON/MATRICE`; a choice; default 'default'; for every step.
Choices: Code_Aster's choice (tangent) (`default`), Tangent (`TANGENTE`), Elastic (`ELASTIQUE`).

Tangent converges in few iterations; elastic is cheaper per iteration and steadier when the tangent misleads (softening).

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:reac_incr -->
### Tangent matrix at increments

`reac_incr`, the solver's `NEWTON/REAC_INCR`; an integer; default 1; in increments; for every step; shown at the power-user level.

At an increment's start the matrix is rebuilt every n-th increment.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:cutback_parts -->
### Cut-back into

`cutback_parts`, the solver's `ECHEC/SUBD_PAS`; an integer; default 4; in parts; for every step.

A failed increment is cut into this many smaller ones.

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:cutback_levels -->
### Cut-backs per increment

`cutback_levels`, the solver's `ECHEC/SUBD_NIVEAU`; an integer; default 5; for every step.

How many times an increment may be cut in turn before the solve stops (5 cuts in 4 = 1/1024 of an increment).

<!-- key: setting:code_aster:absolute_tolerance -->
### Absolute residual

`absolute_tolerance`, the solver's `CONVERGENCE/RESI_GLOB_MAXI`; a number; in N; for every step; shown at the power-user level.

Converged when the largest residual force is below this, in place of the relative tolerance: for loads that are all imposed displacements, or an interface that opens everywhere.

<!-- key: setting:code_saturne -->
## Code_Saturne

<!-- key: setting:code_saturne:pressure_solver -->
### Pressure solver

`pressure_solver`, the solver's `solver_choice (pressure)`; a choice; default 'automatic'; for every step.
Choices: Automatic (Code_Saturne's choice) (`automatic`), Multigrid (`multigrid`), Conjugate gradient (`conjugate_gradient`), BiCGStab (`bi_cgstab`), GMRES (`gmres`), Gauss-Seidel (`gauss_seidel`), Symmetric Gauss-Seidel (`symmetric_gauss_seidel`).

<!-- key: setting:code_saturne:velocity_solver -->
### Velocity solver

`velocity_solver`, the solver's `solver_choice (velocity)`; a choice; default 'automatic'; for every step.
Choices: Automatic (Code_Saturne's choice) (`automatic`), Multigrid (`multigrid`), Conjugate gradient (`conjugate_gradient`), BiCGStab (`bi_cgstab`), GMRES (`gmres`), Gauss-Seidel (`gauss_seidel`), Symmetric Gauss-Seidel (`symmetric_gauss_seidel`).

<!-- key: setting:code_saturne:velocity_scheme -->
### Velocity convection scheme

`velocity_scheme`, the solver's `order_scheme (velocity)`; a choice; default 'automatic'; for every step; shown at the power-user level.
Choices: Automatic (`automatic`), Centred (second order) (`centered`), Second-order linear upwind (SOLU) (`solu`).

How momentum is carried: centred is accurate but can oscillate at high Péclet numbers; SOLU is the robust second order.

<!-- key: setting:elmer -->
## Elmer

<!-- key: setting:elmer:linear_method -->
### Linear solver

`linear_method`, the solver's `Linear System Solver`; a choice; default 'default'; for every step.
Choices: Puzzle's choice for each solver (`default`), Direct (UMFPACK) (`direct`), BiCGStab(l), iterative (`BiCGStabL`), Conjugate gradient, iterative (symmetric systems) (`CG`), GCR, iterative (`GCR`).

Every solver section's linear system (the magnetic A-V solve keeps its direct method: iterative ones stall on it).

<!-- key: setting:elmer:preconditioner -->
### Preconditioner

`preconditioner`, the solver's `Linear System Preconditioning`; a choice; default 'default'; for every step; shown at the power-user level.
Choices: Puzzle's choice (ILU1) (`default`), ILU0 (`ILU0`), ILU1 (`ILU1`), ILU2 (`ILU2`), Diagonal (Jacobi) (`Diagonal`), None (`None`).

For iterative methods: ILU levels trade memory for iterations.

<!-- key: setting:elmer:relaxation -->
### Relaxation factor

`relaxation`, the solver's `Nonlinear System Relaxation Factor`; a number; default 1.0; at most 1; for every step.

Each nonlinear iteration moves this fraction of the way to its new solution: below 1 steadies an iteration that oscillates.

<!-- key: setting:elmer:newton_after_iterations -->
### Newton after

`newton_after_iterations`, the solver's `Nonlinear System Newton After Iterations`; an integer; in iterations; for every step.

Switch from fixed-point (Picard) iterations to Newton after this many: Picard is robust far from the answer, Newton fast near it.

<!-- key: setting:elmer:newton_after_tolerance -->
### Newton below

`newton_after_tolerance`, the solver's `Nonlinear System Newton After Tolerance`; a number; for every step; shown at the power-user level.

Switch to Newton once the change between iterations is below this.

<!-- key: setting:fenicsx -->
## FEniCSx

<!-- key: setting:fenicsx:linear_method -->
### Linear solver

`linear_method`, the solver's `PETSc ksp_type/pc_type`; a choice; default 'lu'; for every step.
Choices: LU, direct (MUMPS where PETSc has it) (`lu`), Conjugate gradient + algebraic multigrid (large symmetric) (`cg_gamg`), Conjugate gradient + Jacobi (`cg_jacobi`), GMRES + algebraic multigrid (`gmres_gamg`).

Each field's own solve; iterative ones need PETSc (not in the Windows build).

<!-- key: setting:opencourant -->
## OpenCourant

OpenCourant has no settings of its own yet.

<!-- key: setting:openfoam -->
## OpenFOAM

<!-- key: setting:openfoam:p_solver -->
### Pressure solver

`p_solver`, the solver's `fvSolution solvers/p`; a choice; default 'GAMG'; for every step.
Choices: GAMG (multigrid) (`GAMG`), PCG (conjugate gradient, DIC) (`PCG`).

<!-- key: setting:openfoam:U_solver -->
### Velocity solver

`U_solver`, the solver's `fvSolution solvers/U`; a choice; default 'smoothSolver'; for every step.
Choices: Smooth solver (symmetric Gauss-Seidel) (`smoothSolver`), PBiCGStab (DILU) (`PBiCGStab`).

<!-- key: setting:openfoam:relaxation_U -->
### Velocity relaxation

`relaxation_U`, the solver's `relaxationFactors U`; a number; default 0.9; for every step; shown at the power-user level.

SIMPLE's under-relaxation of the velocity: lower is steadier, slower.

<!-- key: setting:pynite -->
## PyNite
